newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Nearly 40 hurt in Bangladesh strike violence.
newsitem.headline: Nearly 40 hurt in Bangladesh strike violence.

text.p: Bomb blasts and clashes between rival activists wounded nearly 40 people during an opposition-led general strike on Tuesday in the Bangladesh port of Chittagong and neighbouring areas, police said.
Activists of main opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) exchanged gunfire and fought sporadic battles with supporters of the ruling Awami League, police said.

The BNP supporters ransacked railway offices, damaged a locomotive and attacked an Awami League office, witnesses said. "Up to 40 people have been injured and police arrested at least 15 activists," one police officer in Chittagong said.

Witnesses and officials said business came to a virtual standstill across southeast Bangladesh because of the strike. Trains, ferries and buses were halted, transport operators said. But flights from Dhaka were running on schedule, they said.
Chittagong Stock Exchange, commercial centres, industries, educational institutions, banks and most of the government and private offices were closed.
BNP chief Begum Khaleda Zia called the dawn-to-dusk stoppage to protest against what she said was "government-led terrorism and the ruling party's subservient policies towards India".
